Strait of Hormuz Status: October 14, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  227 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
14 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.99 + 0.95 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Al Jazeera reports attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have soared, with Iran intensifying surveillance and oil flows crashing again.

02 Iran's Guards claim a container ship carrying 2,500 containers sank after striking a mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz; no major wire in this feed carries this independently.

03 Brent stood at $105.99, up 0.95% over 24 hours, as of 12:09 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the focal point of an accelerating maritime crisis, with Al Jazeera reporting that ships in the strait are experiencing the worst spate of attacks since the start of the war and that Iran has stepped up surveillance as oil flows crash again; The Diplomatic Insight separately reports Iran is shifting tactics in its attacks on vessels around the strait. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim a container ship carrying 2,500 containers sank after striking a mine in the southern strait, a claim carried by The Independent and Yahoo News UK among others, though no major wire in this feed carries it independently. An oil tanker fire in the eastern strait was reported by news.sbs.co.krı, which attributes the account to the Iranian Navy, and The Maritime Executive reports two further ship strikes in the strait; these incidents extend a pattern covered in earlier reporting and no row above links them to a single sequence. Brent crude stood at $105.99, up 0.95% over 24 hours, as of 12:09 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, a fraction of the pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The feed indexed 70 headlines in the last 24 hours. Iran's foreign ministry said it is still reviewing the US reply to its seven conditions and will respond through intermediaries, and Mohsen Rezaei has called that reply insufficient, leaving no resolution in sight. As of 12:22 UTC, 91 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
